forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260328225601_f19c6e91
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For every integer n>1, every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, and every real t with m/n <= t < (m+1)/n, one has f_n(t) <= g_n(m).

payload.role_in_assembly: This is the substantive comparison lemma; once t is known to lie in [0,1), the final bound follows after replacing floor(n * t) by m.

floor is applied to real numbers and returns an integer
